answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new agent identity to post a stake that is slashed if the agent is proven to forge signals, so flooding the network with fake selves becomes expensive: an attacker spinning up a jetty of pseudonymous agents, each one a thin thread of apparent consensus, must lock capital in every wallet, and when peers detect coordinated forgery the jade-like collateral is burned or confiscated, raising the marginal cost per fake agent until the attack loses money and honest signaling dominates.
